text:
Olivia (product): Quick sync – we need a concrete prioritization for the long-term routing/tenant isolation work. Main asks on the table: per-tenant isolation lanes (soft vs hard), routing policy templates (latency vs cost), and multi-region failover with tenant affinity. Customers pushing: Acme (compliance + SLA), Nimbus (throughput). Need launch criteria and a migration path. Thoughts?

Mike (eng-arch): My vote is a phased approach. Phase 1: policy templates + guardrails (low risk). Phase 2: soft isolation (logical slices + quotas + canary). Phase 3: hard isolation (dedicated pools, reserved capacity) gated by contracts. Estimated timeline 3–9 months depending on staffing.

Jiang (eng-runtime): From runtime side: soft isolation requires scheduler changes, tenant-level quotas, and safe eviction hooks. We also need KV-cache namespace separation (or eviction boundaries) so noisy tenants don't poison others. Hard isolation implies routing + capacity planner changes and billing hooks. Rough estimates: design 3–4w, impl 6–10w per phase.

Tara (customer-success): FYI Acme wants hard isolation by EOY and will push for a contractual SLA if we can't commit. Nimbus is fine with staged rollouts if we document fallbacks. We should capture explicit acceptance tests.

Alex (security): Must include crypto separation (tenant keys), audit log retention, and a documented threat model. Pen test required before GA for any "hard isolation" offering.

Olivia (product): Draft launch criteria suggestion: 1) Per-tenant P95 latency <99.9% under committed load; 2) Clear failover semantics (regional affinity + fallback policy) documented; 3) Migration runbook + rollback; 4) KMS + audit enabled for isolated tenants; 5) Canary with 2 customers and performance/regressions guarded. Agree?

Mike (eng-arch): :thumbsup: add autoscaling and capacity-saturation tests to that list. Also define cost guardrails so we don't blow unit economics when cache isolation reduces hit rate.

Jiang (eng-runtime): Agreed. We should add a metric for prefix-cache hit-rate and per-tenant batching efficiency to the success criteria. If hit-rate drops > X% we need an automated mitigation (e.g., hybrid cache or burst credits).

Tara (customer-success): Also add customer acceptance criteria: Acme acceptance test pass + signed amendment for hard isolation SLA. Nimbus to be included in soft isolation canary.

Olivia (product): Action items: Mike + Jiang — write tech spec with sequence diagrams, rollout plan, and gating criteria by Monday. Tara — confirm Acme desired dates and identify canary tenants. Alex — surface threat model and compliance checklist. I'll consolidate and propose prioritization at next arch sync. Anyone else?

infra-bot: Deployed checklist template v0.2 to #eng-infra: https://internal.redwood/checklists/routing-isolation-v0.2

Mike (eng-arch): Putting a placeholder PR: https://github.com/redwood/specs/pull/123 with initial sketch (WIP).

Olivia (product): If no objections I'll mark "policy templates + soft isolation" as high priority and gate hard isolation on contract commitments and capacity funding. Sync Wed 10:00 in #architecture. Thanks everyone.

---

Olivia (product) added an example routing policy snippet:

```
routing_policy:
  - match: region=eu
    prefer: low_latency
  - match: tenant=acme
    isolation: dedicated_pool
```

Olivia (product): Notes: the snippet is illustrative; real policy needs schema, validation, and simulator before rollout.

Jiang (eng-runtime): I'll add simulator tests to the spec to validate policy interactions with batching and cache behavior.

Tara (customer-success): I'll draft an acceptance test template for Acme to sign off on.

Olivia (product): Great. Meeting capture will go to the roadmap doc after spec PR lands.
